# Results — Study 344 (Backtest-Overfitting): the trap, measured

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The study is a **research-method
demo**: we run a grid of long/flat moving-average crossover rules (the "researcher's parameter
zoo") on tapes we control, pick the in-sample champion, and watch it out-of-sample — then put a
number on the trap with the **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** (DSR) and the **Probability of Backtest
Overfitting** (PBO, via CSCV). The synthetic core is offline and deterministic; one real worked
example uses SPY. As-of **2026-05-31** (SPY through the last full month; the in-progress June bar
is dropped). Match the fingerprints to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamps

| Tape | Span | n | Fingerprint | Source |
|---|---|--:|---|---|
| Synthetic NULL (`edge=0`) | 1,260 trading days | 1,260 | `2abc7518fe78` | deterministic GRW, seed 344 |
| Synthetic CONTROL (`edge=0.0003`) | 1,260 trading days | 1,260 | — | deterministic GRW, seed 344 |
| Real SPY (total-return) | 2000-01-03 → 2026-05-29 | 6,641 | `022e57e68917` | Yahoo! Finance, auto-adjusted |

Grid: **1,000** crossover configurations (`fast`, `slow`) with `fast < slow`, swept on each tape.
In-sample / out-of-sample split = first 50% / last 50%. PBO via CSCV with S = 10 blocks
(C(10,5) = 252 symmetric partitions).

## The headline — the null tape, where we KNOW there is no edge

On a pure martingale (`edge = 0`), no timing rule can have any edge; everything the grid finds is
luck. Yet:

| Quantity | Value | Reading |
|---|--:|---|
| In-sample Sharpe of the champion | **+0.88** | "a gorgeous backtest" |
| Out-of-sample Sharpe of that champion | **−0.49** | the live disappointment |
| OOS HAC *t* of the champion | **−0.77** | indistinguishable from zero (correctly) |
| Expected max Sharpe under the null, SR₀ (N = 1000) | **3.26** | the bar luck alone clears |
| **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** | **≈ 0.00** | the 0.88 is *below* what luck delivers |
| **PBO (CSCV)** | **0.68** | the IS winner is an OOS loser 68% of the time |

The IS champion looks like a Sharpe-0.88 strategy and is, with certainty, nothing. The DSR sees
straight through it (the best of 1000 trials should clear Sharpe ≈ 3.3 by luck alone, so 0.88 is
*unimpressive*), and PBO = 0.68 says the selection process is **worse than a coin flip**.

## The expected-max-Sharpe bar climbs with the number of trials

The more configurations you try, the higher the luckiest Sharpe — this is the whole disease:

| N trials | Champion IS Sharpe | Champion OOS Sharpe | SR₀ (expected max, null) | DSR |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 | +0.65 | −0.37 | 1.57 | 0.00 |
| 50 | +0.88 | −0.49 | 2.28 | 0.00 |
| 200 | +0.88 | −0.49 | 2.77 | 0.00 |
| 1000 | +0.88 | −0.49 | 3.26 | 0.00 |

SR₀ rises from 1.6 to 3.3 as the trial count goes 10 → 1000. A naked Sharpe that would impress at
N = 10 is *noise* at N = 1000 — which is why a Sharpe must always be reported with the number of
trials behind it.

## The positive control — a real but un-timeable edge

On a tape with a tiny *constant drift* (`edge = 0.0003/day`, a real ~8%/yr trend that accrues to
**buy-and-hold**, not to any timing rule), the diagnostics behave exactly as a faithful detector
should:

| Strategy | Sharpe | DSR | PBO |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold (one honest hypothesis, N = 1) | 0.92 | **0.98** | — |
| Grid-searched timing champion (N = 1000) | IS 1.19 → OOS 0.03 | **0.00** | **0.80** |

The single honest hypothesis (own the asset) survives with DSR 0.98 — because it was *not*
selected from a zoo. The grid-searched timing champion, even riding the same real drift, collapses
out of sample (IS 1.19 → OOS 0.03) and the diagnostics flag it: DSR ≈ 0, PBO = 0.80. **The trap is
in the *selection*, not in the existence of an edge.**

## The real worked example — SPY 2000–2026

The same grid-search on SPY, IS = 2000–2013, OOS = 2013–2026:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Champion (`fast`, `slow`) | `f10_s188` |
| Champion IS Sharpe | +0.68 |
| Champion OOS Sharpe | +0.81 |
| OOS HAC *t* | +3.10 |
| **DSR (N = 1000)** | **≈ 0.00** |
| **PBO (CSCV)** | **0.60** |
| SPY buy-and-hold Sharpe | 0.51 |
| Buy-and-hold DSR (N = 1) | 0.996 |

Here the champion's OOS Sharpe held up (0.81) — but **that is the danger**, not the reassurance.
The OOS HAC *t* = 3.1 is market *beta*: a long-biased rule rode the 2013–2026 bull, exactly as
buy-and-hold did. The overfitting diagnostics warn you anyway — DSR ≈ 0 (the IS Sharpe never
cleared the 3.26 bar from 1000 trials) and PBO = 0.60 (selection worse than a coin) — because a
single lucky OOS run is *not* evidence the selection generalises. Meanwhile honest buy-and-hold
posts DSR 0.996. The lesson: one out-of-sample window can lie; the deflation and PBO cannot be
talked out of by a good outcome.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** By construction the synthetic timing edge is zero, and the in-sample Sharpe of
  the selected champion deflates to DSR ≈ 0 on every tape. On real SPY the champion's apparent
  out-of-sample success is long-only market beta, not timing skill (and its DSR is still ≈ 0). There
  is no robust *t* ≥ 2 attributable to *selection* anywhere; the only thing that earns is owning the
  asset.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to trade. The gorgeous in-sample Sharpe is an artefact
  of trying many configurations; out of sample it is gone (null tape) or is repackaged beta (SPY).
- **Does grid-searching a backtest manufacture a false edge? — CONFIRMED.** On a tape we *know* is
  empty, a 1000-rule sweep produces an IS Sharpe of 0.88 that is pure luck; DSR ≈ 0 and PBO = 0.68
  expose it, and the positive control shows the diagnostics spare a genuinely honest single
  hypothesis. The trap is real, measurable, and correctable — report DSR and PBO, not a naked Sharpe.
